overview: This Senate resolution recognizes January 2025 as National Mentoring Month, an effort to celebrate mentoring relationships and recruit more mentors for young people. It describes how mentors can help with schoolwork, career goals, mental health, and staying out of trouble, and notes that about 1 in 3 young people grow up without a mentor outside their home. It thanks the staff and volunteers of mentoring programs and supports expanding quality programs and closing that "mentoring gap." The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on February 4, 2025.
for: Supporters say recognizing mentoring draws attention to a low-cost way to help young people succeed and can encourage more adults to volunteer.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not provide any funding or change any law to expand mentoring programs.
